newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin Energy merger still on hold.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin Energy merger still on hold.

text.p: A Dane County Circuit Court judge blocked Wisconsin regulators from considering the proposed merger between Wisconsin Energy Corp and Northern States Power Co until an investigation of allegations of illegal communications between the commission and Wisconsin Energy is completed, regulators said Friday.
"The merger remains on hold," Jeff Butson, a spokesman for the Wisconsin Public Service Commission, told Reuters. "We just want to move forward now with the investigation."

Judge Mark Frankel late Thursday ordered the panel not to hold hearings to consider the $6.0 billion proposal until a complete investigation of the allegations of improper communications between commissioner Daniel Eastman and Wisconsin Energy is conducted, Butson said.

Two consumer advocate groups making the allegations amended their complaints to include two affidavits filed by two employees of Madison Gas & Electric Co indicating that illegal conversations took place, Butson said.
Butson identified the witnesses as Scott Neitzel, a former member of the regulatory commission, who is a consultant to Madison Gas, and Madison Gas executive Mark Williamson.
Neither Neitzel nor Williamson were available to comment Friday, although a Madison Gas spokesman confirmed the men filed affidavits in the case.
Regulators will now decide how the investigation of the allegations will proceed, Butson said.
"They can take the case to either the Dane County district attorney, the (state) attorney general, hire an independent investigator or launch an internal probe," Butson said.

He added that the panel is not expected to decide which option will be taken before next Tuesday, although they are not expected to hold an internal probe to ensure the public remains informed, Butson said.
"We don't believe the affidavits are credible," Wisconsin Energy spokeswoman Maripat Blankenheim said, "and we believe the investigation will bear that out."

Blankenheim also reiterated the utility's contention that no company official had inappropriate meetings or conversations with Eastman, who also denied any wrongdoing and will abstain from participating in the probe.
"We are still as frustrated as the public commission must be," Blankenheim said.
Wisconsin Energy and Minneapolis-based Northern States originally announced the merger, which will create a new company called Primergy Corp, in May of 1995.
